# Joseph Alabi Adewoye Foundation

> A legally registered Nigerian non-governmental organisation (CAC RC 8401335) based in Ijara-Isin, Kwara State. It honours the late Mr. Joseph Alabi Adewoye, a pioneering graphic artist, educator and cultural administrator, by advancing human and environmental development in Ijara-Isin and surrounding communities.

## About the foundation

- Focus areas: education, youth empowerment, arts and cultural heritage, infrastructure, and environmental sustainability in rural communities.
- Vision: to sustain the legacy of Joseph Alabi Adewoye and improve the standard of living through community-focused, creative and developmental initiatives in Ijara-Isin and beyond.
- Mission: to promote human and environmental development by initiating and supporting programmes that foster education, artistic expression, cultural awareness and sustainable community growth.
- Governance: a Board of Trustees made up of Mr. Adewoye's children: Ademola Julius Adewoye, Kayode Adegoke Adewoye, Yetunde Adunni Adewoye, Adeyinka Alabi Adewoye and Babatunde Adebowale Adewoye. The late Olubunmi Akanbi Adewoye, his second child, is remembered alongside them.
- Address: Iji Road, opposite Ijara-Isin Town Hall, Ijara-Isin, Kwara State, Nigeria.
- Email: adewoyefoundation@gmail.com

## About Mr. Joseph Alabi Adewoye

- Born in Ijara, Kwara State. Attended Provincial Secondary School, Ilorin (1959) and Bauchi Teachers College.
- B.A. Fine Arts, Ahmadu Bello University (1965); Cert. S.P.P, London College of Printing (screen printing, airbrushing, typography, package design).
- Graphic Art Officer, Northern Nigeria Ministry of Information; head of the Graphic Art Section, Kwara State Military Governor's Office (1968).
- Lecturer in Graphic Design, Ahmadu Bello University (1973).
- First Artistic Director of the Graphic Arts Division under the Ministry of Culture and Information, and the first Chief Cultural Officer of Kwara State.
- Served on the Niger Art Council and the National Festival Committee; member of the FESTAC '77 planning committee, representing Kwara State.
